title: chenopodium ambrosioides var. suffruticosum
intro: Chenopodium ambrosioides var. suffruticosum, commonly known as Mexican tea or epazote, is a variety of the Chenopodium ambrosioides plant, a member of the amaranth family. This plant is valued for its traditional use in folk medicine, and has been reported to have a range of health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties, which may aid in the treatment of digestive issues and other health conditions. The therapeutic actions of Mexican tea include its ability to stimulate digestion, reduce nausea and vomiting, and exhibit anti-inflammatory and antispasmodic effects. The bioactive constituents of Chenopodium ambrosioides var. suffruticosum include alkaloids, such as ascaridole and chenopodine, as well as volatile oils and other compounds that contribute to its medicinal properties.
